title: The laboratory fault, pushed fast and slow

data.source: Stick-Slip of Granular Fault Gouge Under Different Normal Stresses and Loading Rates, figshare (2026), doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.31047475.v1; glass beads, 5 MPa, 5, 10 and 50 micrometres per second

claim_kind: retrodiction (published laboratory data; mapping and detector frozen before any stress value was analysed)
prediction: A laboratory fault slips after the same amount of push at 5 and at 50 micrometres per second: the slope of log(push per slip) on log(speed) has a 95 % interval inside -0.05 to +0.05.
baseline: The field's own model (faults heal with the logarithm of rest time, so push per slip falls with speed: slope about -0.10 to -0.02, from memory) and a clock decoy (a slip every fixed time, slope +1).
why: Withdrawn after the second check. By the frozen rule the first run said `fails`. But there is one run at each speed, so the slope rests on three points and one degree of freedom, and the runs differ in ways that are not speed. The three runs do differ; nothing ties the difference to speed. Repeat runs agreeing to a few per cent would restore a verdict.

first_run.note: the frozen rule; interval and weight assume the three runs differ only by speed

amended.reason:
AMENDMENT, 2026-11-19, AFTER THE SECOND CHECK (docs/CHECKS_RATE_SECOND_LOOK.md). The frozen docstring is unchanged
and so is its hash. The first run, by the frozen rule, gave `fails` (slope -0.1664, interval -0.1927 to -0.135,
weight of a not-pass 22.1 to 1). That verdict is WITHDRAWN to `untestable`.
Why. The interval covers scatter from slip to slip inside a run, and the weight came from simulated worlds in
which the three runs differ ONLY by speed. But there is one run per speed. The unit of replication for a slope
across speeds is the run: three points, one degree of freedom. The slope through the three run means with that
one degree of freedom has an interval of about -1.4 to +1.1 on this script's run means (computed below; the second
checker, with a slightly different run-in, got -1.65 to +1.33). The middle run took MORE push per
slip than the slow one, and the second checker found the reloading stiffness differs between runs by a third
(4.2, 2.8, 3.9 kPa per micrometre), so the runs differ in ways that are not speed. The second checker's sum: if
packings differ by 10 % the weight of a `fail` drops to 2.7 to 1, under the protocol's 3 to 1.
The frozen docstring had declared this limit; the verdict rule did not follow it. This moves away from `fails`,
as the rt-004 amendment did. It is the withdrawal of a claim, not an upgrade. The first-run verdict and every
first-run number are kept.
What would restore a verdict: published repeat runs at each speed that agree to a few per cent.
Also corrected: the 27 "slips" found in noise come from the random-walk control (it wanders slowly and the zigzag
rule does not require a fall to be sudden), not from the data. The second checker's detector, which requires a
sudden fall, invents none, and 261 of the 262 real slips are falls of more than 100 kPa.
